source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An infant monitored for increased ICP has an anterior fontanel that bulges only when crying. What should the nurse conclude?
options: Lower the head of the bed
questions.rationale: The anterior fontanel is normally soft and flat. A bulging fontanel may come from crying or from increased ICP, so bulging only with crying is normal.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q85 (PDF p. 231)
questions.quote: Remember that a bulging or tense fontanel may result from crying; therefore, it is a normal finding.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: How does the nurse test a child's pharyngeal (gag) reflex?
options: Touch the back of the throat
questions.rationale: The gag reflex is tested by touching the back of the throat with a tongue depressor. Asking the child to swallow tests the swallowing reflex.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q114 (PDF p. 263)
questions.quote: The pharyngeal (gag) reflex is tested by touching the back of the throat with an object, such as a tongue depressor.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Where does the nurse palpate the apical pulse?
questions.rationale: The point of maximal impulse is normally at the fourth or fifth intercostal space at the left midclavicular line.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q179 (PDF p. 332)
questions.quote: The point of maximal impulse (PMI), where the apical pulse is palpated, is normally located in the fourth or fifth intercostal space, at the left midclavicular line.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How are normal bowel sounds described?
questions.rationale: Normal bowel sounds are soft gurgles or clicks occurring irregularly 5 to 35 times a minute. Loud gurgles (borborygmi) mean hyperperistalsis; a swishing sound is a bruit.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q182 (PDF p. 335)
questions.quote: normal bowel sounds are relatively soft gurgling or clicking sounds that occur irregularly 5 to 35 times per minute.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which breath sounds does the nurse expect over the right lower lobe in a client with pneumonia there?
questions.rationale: Consolidated tissue carries bronchial sounds to the periphery, so bronchial sounds are heard over consolidation. Crackles may also be heard.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q225 (PDF p. 380)
questions.quote: The client with pneumonia will have bronchial breath sounds over area(s) of consolidation

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client has smoked three-fourths of a pack a day for 10 years. What is his smoking history?
questions.rationale: Pack-years equal packs per day times years smoked: 0.75 × 10 = 7.5.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q258 (PDF p. 415)
questions.quote: The standard method for quantifying smoking history is to multiply the number of packs smoked per day by the number of years of smoking.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which finding should the school nurse look for when screening for scoliosis?
questions.rationale: Signs include chest asymmetry, unequal rib heights, and lateral deviation and rotation of the vertebrae. Children 9 to 15 are screened; girls are at highest risk.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q618 (PDF p. 833)
questions.quote: Scoliosis is a lateral curvature of the spine.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: How should a child stand for scoliosis screening?
questions.rationale: The child stands in underpants with weight on both feet, legs straight, and arms hanging loosely so the chest, back, and hips are seen clearly.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1168 (PDF p. 1455)
questions.quote: The child is asked to stand with weight equally on both feet with the legs straight and the arms hanging loosely at both sides.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which woman is at GREATEST risk for osteoporosis?
questions.rationale: Asian, white, small-boned, and fair-skinned women are at highest risk. Early menopause and a family history add to the risk.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q630 (PDF p. 847)
questions.quote: Asian, white, small-boned, and fair-skinned women are at greatest risk for osteoporosis.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which statement about breast self-examination needs correction?
options: 'I can use soapy hands in the shower.'
'I check in front of a mirror.'
'I do it on the first day of my period.'
questions.rationale: BSE is done 2 or 3 days after menstruation ends, when breasts are least tender. Lumps, including in the armpit, and nipple discharge are reported.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q654 (PDF p. 872)
questions.quote: The examination is performed 2 or 3 days after menstruation ends, when the breasts are least likely to be tender and swollen.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Two months after a right mastectomy, a client says she has not done BSE on her left breast. Which coping mechanism is she likely using?
questions.rationale: Denying or minimizing a health problem can lead to avoiding self-care such as BSE, which can be life-threatening.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q947 (PDF p. 1192)
questions.quote: Denial can lead to an avoidance of self-care measures, such as taking medications or performing a BSE.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which statement about testicular self-examination needs MORE teaching?
options: 'I'll do it after a warm shower.'
'A cord-like part in back is normal.'
questions.rationale: TSE is done monthly. After a warm shower the scrotum is relaxed, and the spermatic cord is a normal finding.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1078 (PDF p. 1360)
questions.quote: TSE should be performed every month.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which instruction belongs in a high school class on testicular self-examination?
options: Do it after a cold shower
questions.rationale: TSE screens for testicular cancer, common in late teens and twenties. It is done monthly after a warm shower, rolling each testicle between thumb and fingers.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1369 (PDF p. 1672)
questions.quote: TSE is a self-screening examination for testicular cancer, which predominantly affects men in their late teens and twenties.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should the nurse test for asterixis in hepatic encephalopathy?
questions.rationale: Asterixis (liver flap) is a rapid, nonrhythmic tremor of the wrists and fingers, seen when the client extends the arm, wrist, and fingers.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q684 (PDF p. 905)
questions.quote: Asterixis is a rapid, nonrhythmic, abnormal muscle tremor of the wrists and fingers that is commonly associated with hepatic encephalopathy

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: To test cranial nerve XII after a stroke, what does the nurse ask the client to do?
questions.rationale: Cranial nerve XII (hypoglossal) controls the tongue, so the nurse checks the ability to extend the tongue.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q685 (PDF p. 906)
questions.quote: To assess the function of cranial nerve XII (hypoglossal), the nurse should assess the client’s ability to extend the tongue.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding is related to cranial nerve III (oculomotor) dysfunction?
questions.rationale: CN III controls pupil constriction and upper eyelid elevation; pressure on it causes ptosis. The others are early signs of a falling level of consciousness.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1122 (PDF p. 1406)
questions.quote: Ptosis of the eyelid is caused by pressure on and the dysfunction of cranial nerve III, the oculomotor nerve.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: To assess the limbic system in a client with dementia, what should the nurse assess?
questions.rationale: The limbic system governs feelings and emotions. Judgment is frontal lobe, consciousness is the reticular activating system, and eye movements are CN III, IV, and VI.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1003 (PDF p. 1254)
questions.quote: Feelings and emotions are part of the role of the limbic system.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After shoulder arthroplasty, how does the nurse check the ULNAR nerve?
questions.rationale: Spreading the fingers wide against pressure tests the ulnar nerve. A grasp that tests the first and second fingers checks the median nerve.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q735 (PDF p. 960)
questions.quote: the client is asked to spread all of the fingers wide and resist pressure. Weakness against pressure may indicate compromise of the ulnar nerve.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After shoulder arthroplasty, how does the nurse check the MEDIAN nerve?
questions.rationale: The client grasps the nurse's hand while the nurse notes the strength of the first and second fingers. A weak grip may mean median nerve compromise.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1520 (PDF p. 1830)
questions.quote: To assess the median nerve status, the client should be instructed to grasp the nurse’s hand.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A woman with a family history of hypertension is screened. Which finding needs teaching on stroke prevention?
questions.rationale: Oral contraceptives promote clot formation. They, along with obesity, hypertension, high cholesterol, and smoking, are modifiable stroke risk factors.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q688 (PDF p. 909)
questions.quote: The use of oral contraceptives, obesity, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and smoking are all modifiable risk factors for stroke.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which lab finding is MOST important to modify to lower the risk of coronary artery disease?
questions.rationale: LDL is more directly linked with CAD than other lipoproteins and predicts it better than triglycerides. Lipase is a digestive enzyme.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q689 (PDF p. 910)
questions.quote: LDLs are more directly associated with CAD than are other lipoproteins.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A 39-year-old Filipino man has BP 152/92 at rest, cholesterol 180 mg/dL, and fasting glucose 90 mg/dL. Which CAD risk factor is the priority?
questions.rationale: Hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor. His cholesterol and glucose are normal, and age over 40 is nonmodifiable.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1133 (PDF p. 1418)
questions.quote: Hypertension, cigarette smoking, and hyperlipidemia are major risk modifiable factors for coronary artery disease.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which assessment gives the BEST information about left-sided heart function?
questions.rationale: Left-sided failure backs fluid into the lungs, so breath sounds reflect it. Edema, hepatojugular reflux, and JVD are right-sided signs.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1098 (PDF p. 1382)
questions.quote: The assessment of breath sounds provides information about left-sided heart function.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: In a pregnant client with heart disease, where is venous congestion MOST commonly seen?
questions.rationale: Venous congestion that can become varicosities is most often seen in the legs, vulva, or rectum. Edema of the fingers or eyes is not directly venous congestion.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1106 (PDF p. 1390)
questions.quote: Venous congestion is most commonly noted in the legs, the vulva, or the rectum.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding is a positive Kernig's sign in a child?
options: Cannot fully extend the legs supine
Hips flex when the neck flexes
questions.rationale: Kernig's sign is the inability to extend the legs fully while supine. Brudzinski's sign is hip flexion when the neck is flexed. Both suggest bacterial meningitis.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1111 (PDF p. 1395)
questions.quote: Kernig’s sign is the inability of the child to extend the legs fully when lying supine.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which factor should the nurse consider when teaching a child about his illness?
options: Older children have shorter attention spans
Imagination may cause more fear than truth
questions.rationale: Teaching is adjusted to the child's age and cognition. A child's imagination may create more fear than the truth, and a child may regress when ill.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q740 (PDF p. 966)
questions.quote: the nurse needs to adjust the complexity and volume of information based on the child’s age and cognitive level.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which is a cause of ORGANIC erectile dysfunction?
questions.rationale: Organic causes include hypertension, vascular disease, diabetes, and alcohol. Stress, depression, and anxiety are psychogenic causes.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q785 (PDF p. 1015)
questions.quote: Organic erectile dysfunction is a gradual deterioration of function

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding can percussion identify?
questions.rationale: Percussion assesses the size, borders, and consistency of organs and detects fluid in body cavities. Palpation assesses mobility, temperature, and resilience.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q797 (PDF p. 1027)
questions.quote: Percussion involves tapping the body with the fingertips to evaluate the size, borders, and consistency of body organs and assess for fluid in body cavities.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which factor places an older adult MOST at risk for abuse?
questions.rationale: Elder abuse may come from frustrated adult children caring for dependent parents. Growing demands can cause resentment. Abuse is not tied to income level.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q831 (PDF p. 1067)
questions.quote: Elder abuse is sometimes the result of frustrated adult children who find themselves caring for dependent parents.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which action by a new nurse auscultating breath sounds needs correction?
questions.rationale: Breath sounds are heard with the warmed diaphragm on bare skin while the client sits up and breathes slowly and deeply through the mouth.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1280 (PDF p. 1581)
questions.quote: The bell of the stethoscope is not used to auscultate breath sounds.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After suctioning a tracheostomy, which finding BEST shows the procedure worked?
questions.rationale: Breath sounds show how well the airways were cleared of secretions. The other parameters are less precise for this purpose.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1319 (PDF p. 1621)
questions.quote: the breath sounds are auscultated to determine the extent to which the airways have been cleared of respiratory secretions.
